newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland to get 600 new Jobs in Dublin and Galway.
newsitem.headline: Ireland to get 600 new Jobs in Dublin and Galway.

text.p: Minister for Enterprise and Employment, Richard Bruton on Wednesday said that up to 600 new jobs will be created by four IDA-Ireland backed companies.
Bruton said 300 of the new jobs will be created by the expansion of Japanese company KAO Corporation in it's production of CD-ROMs in Clondalkin and it's teleservices operation in Ballsbridge.
He said a further 100 jobs will be in the newly established Telenor, a Norwegian telecommunications company setting up a software development operation in Dublin.

German travel giant DER will create 175 new jobs in a new shared services and teleservicing operation in the IDA Business Park, Galway and 21 new jobs will be created by Rood Technology in Dublin in production support services for the electronics industry."

Bruton said that the mix of activities - production, teleservices, and software development - will provide employment for a wide range of people from factory floor employees to men and women with language skills and graduates with the most sophisticated engineering qualifications.
